post.caption:
2 suitcases for a 5-day trip. What have you packed for Allah? 🧳

Thursday, 5:40 p.m. The ferry to your grandfather. Two bags full of chargers, gifts and shoes you won’t even wear. An old man at the rail with one small bag and a tasbih: “My bag is light. I sent the rest ahead.”

“And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion.” (57:20)

Tonight, before Isha: one good deed no one will see.

captions: Thursday, 5:40 p.m. The ferry to your grandfather. 40 minutes across.
Two bags. Chargers, gifts, shoes you won’t even wear.
Gulls follow the boat. You film them for your story.
An old man at the rail. One small bag. A tasbih in his hand.
The horn. “Arriving in ten minutes.” Everyone grabs their things.
He smiles. “My bag is light. I sent the rest ahead.”
You look at your two bags. Then at your empty hands.
Morning. Grandpa’s olive grove. He planted it at twenty.
“The first trees fed other people,” he says. “Not me.”
“That’s how you pack for the long trip.”
Your hands are full of olives now. You know what to send ahead.
